One word ('Rahmqvists samband' or 'Rahmqvists fynd') removes both the passage friction and the internal mismatch.

findings.claim: The structural gap named in round 2 is still open — every repair round writes new student-facing Swedish downstream of the language stage — and this round's prose contains one calque that is unique in the entire LÄS corpus.
findings.evidence: reviews/language.jsonl for this unit is dated 11:16; the Q2 rationale was written wholesale at 12:29 and edited again at 12:41, and the Q1/Q3/Q4 rationales at 11:51. Q3's rationale reads 'att stammen nämner Sandells ämne räcker alltså inte för att peka ut svaret' — bare 'stammen' as a calque of English 'stem' (native: 'frågan' / 'frågestammen'; bare 'stammen' reads as trunk/stem of a plant). A corpus-wide scan of every LÄS candidate in batches 1–13 returns exactly ONE occurrence of 'stammen' in a rationale — this one. The new Q2 rationale also has 'A, B och D namnger omständigheter som mycket väl kan dra ut på ett tornbygge' — 'namnger' takes a name-bearer in Swedish; 'anger' or 'nämner' is the native verb here. EXPLICITLY NOT FLAGGED: 'hedgat' (32 corpus hits), 'hedgning' (11) and the English trap labels reversed_causality / plausible_worldknowledge / overgeneralisation / detail_as_main (446 hits across all 13 batches) are a fleet-wide house convention, not a defect of this unit; round 2's structural point should not be read as covering them.
findings.why: The rationale is the teaching payload. Neither item is a comprehension barrier and the round-2 ungrammatical clause ('men inte över vad höjden ska räknas') died with the retargeted Q2, so this drops from minor to note — but the ordering gap that produced both is unchanged: BATCH-RUNBOOK's stage table has no language pass downstream of pedagogy, and integrated's brief is cross-part consistency, not native register.
